report: NOT WRITTEN: the subagent harness refused to create /Users/tj/software/terrain-work/body-look/ffm-losses/high-orbit/REPORT.md, so the findings are in the mechanisms, fixes and unsettled fields of this output. Tables are in /Users/tj/software/terrain-work/body-look/ffm-losses/high-orbit/tables.md (every GD/GE/IG loss row, and GN/WA per satellite, arc and lead) and /Users/tj/software/terrain-work/body-look/ffm-losses/high-orbit/reruns.md (all 57 rerun rows). Raw rows are in rows-*.jsonl, diverge-lageos1-1122.json, diverge2-lageos1-1122.json and burns-waas-hourly.json in the same directory. Scripts are in /Users/tj/software/terrain-work/body-look/ffm-losses/high-orbit/scripts/ (host2.mjs, fit2.mjs, rerun.mjs, diverge.mjs, diverge2.mjs, burn-times.mjs, build.py).

mechanisms.claim: GD (LAGEOS 1, LAGEOS 2, LARES-2) losses come from the integrator setting: steps capped at 300 s on an orbit with a 3.8 h period. The physics is not the cause. Etalon (11.3 h period) never loses (0 of 22 at day 7).
mechanisms.evidence: One fitted LAGEOS 1 state (2025-11-22) was flown as pure two-body at (300 s, 1e-8). Against (30 s, 1e-10) it drifts 6.3 / 13.0 / 32.0 m along-track at days 1 / 3 / 7. The drift is the same with J2 only, 20x20, third bodies or SRP (diverge2-lageos1-1122.json). Tolerance 1e-10 at 300 s still gives 20.8 m at day 7 (rows-test.jsonl tol10). Steps of 120 s bring day-7 FFM error below AP on 7 of 8 windows (e.g. LAGEOS 1 2025-11-22: 23.9 to 3.7 m, AP 5.3; LAGEOS 2 2025-10-11: 33.7 to 8.2 m, AP 10.0; LARES-2 2025-11-08: 46.0 to 22.1 m, AP 24.4). With tides and 30 s steps, 4 of 5 windows beat AP at day 7 (LAGEOS 2 2025-11-08: 44.0 to 1.0 m, AP 13.8); the one that doesn't, LAGEOS 1 2025-11-22, is 6.5 m against AP 5.3. Where the setting comes from: ffmHigh, all-regimes.mjs:37-41 and truth-compare.mjs:34-38, applied to every orbit with r >= 8400 km (all-regimes.mjs:128). AP6.md:26 cites CHEAPER.md, but CHEAPER claimed this setting for navigation only. Its geodetic report showed full FFM 0.003 km against 0.018 km at 168 h. Shadow is not the cause: LAGEOS's first shadow is at forecast hour 114.7, and the drift is already 14 m by hour 81 in a flight with no shadow (diverge-lageos1-1122.json).

mechanisms.claim: GD second-order: solid tides are off in the high-orbit setting. This leaves FFM's normal error near 3 m at every lead.
mechanisms.evidence: Turning solidTides on takes normal error from about 3.1 m to 0.2-0.4 m at all leads (LAGEOS 1 2025-11-22; tides and tides30 runs). AP has no tides either; its normal error is 3-4 m. Tides with the 300 s step alone makes day-7 along-track worse (31.9 m), so the step error dominates. Other forces, tested on one window only (LAGEOS 1 2025-11-22): IERS 2010 relativity changes nothing (23.92 against 23.94 m), Knocke albedo/IR changes nothing (24.04 m), and 70x70 gravity is no better than 20x20 at a 30 s step (6.55 m both).

mechanisms.claim: GE and IG (BeiDou and QZSS GEO and IGSO) losses come from the force model. Cannonball SRP has no once-per-revolution terms, and these orbit-normal or fixed-yaw buses need them. FFM's full-state fit absorbs the missing signal into its semimajor axis and eccentricity, so the along-track error grows quadratically. AP's mean-element fit does not do that, so AP's error grows linearly.
mechanisms.evidence: On C020 2025-10-08, the cannonball fit leaves about 2.9 m per axis (reduced chi-square 0.086 at 10 m). A 168 h arc is worse: chi-square 0.94 and day 7 at 0.38 km. Fitting cannonball plus ECOM2 Y0, B0, B1c and B1s (ecom5) gives chi-square 0.0037 and errors of 3.2 / 7.4 / 11.4 / 62.0 m at days 1 / 2 / 3 / 7, against AP's 19.8 / 26.8 / 36.8 / 92.3 m. ecom5 beats AP at every lead on all 9 GE and IG windows tested: C020 10-04 (day 7 8.5 against 106.7 m), C217 10-10 (8.1 against 33.2), C006 10-08 (87.4 against 148.1), C011 10-06 (44.1 against 141.3), C221, C009, C220, and J004 QZS-2I 10-12 (day 1 1.3 against 15.7 m). Fitted B1 terms are 4-6.6e-9 m/s^2 on BDS-2 GEO. Things that do not fix it, at day 7 on C020 10-08: Y0 alone 183 m, constant in-track 169 m, B0 alone 262 m, D2c alone 265 m, and full settings (70x70, tides, relativity, 1e-10, 120 s) 261.5 m against the stored 262.1 m. AP's AGOM (0.0246) equals FFM's fitted SRP (0.0245), so AP's AGOM does not soak up a force FFM lacks. The shadow is ruled out as the cause: AP treats the GEO eclipse season as wholly sunlit (sdn-ap SPEC.md:574-575) and still wins. FFM's conical shadow is hard-coded (propagator/ffm/lib/force_models.cpp:471-472), and ECOM2 fixes the losses without changing it. The truth for these groups is GFZ's multi-GNSS rapid orbit (GFZ0MGXRAP, sources.mjs:139-144), not ESA finals.

mechanisms.claim: GN: the losses on Galileo FOC E218 (43058), 334 of the 498 GN loss rows, come from the settled FOC Y-bias. Cannonball SRP has no force along the Y axis.
mechanisms.evidence: Holding Y0 at +6.85e-10 m/s^2 (results/ffm-galileo-y-bias) or fitting ecom5 removes the loss at every lead on 3 of 3 windows. Day-7 errors, held Y0 / ecom5 / stored FFM / AP: 72 h arc 2026-04-16: 7.2 / 2.2 / 135.0 / 40.0 m; 72 h arc 2026-04-14: 8.7 / 7.4 / 165.0 / 48.9 m; 24 h arc 2026-04-16: 6.4 / 5.4 / 98.1 / 40.1 m. The freely fitted Y0 comes out at 6.9-7.6e-10, matching the published FOC value.

mechanisms.claim: GN: the GPS and GLONASS losses (164 rows, mostly day 7 on 72 h arcs) have the same cause: cannonball SRP.
mechanisms.evidence: ecom5 beats AP at every lead on the two windows tested. GPS IIR-M 28874 2026-01-03: day 7 1.9 m against AP 15.6 m (stored FFM 35.7). GLONASS-M 37869 2026-05-28: 13.7 m against 33.4 m (stored 61.2). The other GPS and GLONASS windows are classed by group, not tested one by one.

mechanisms.claim: WA ties at ratio 1.00 because both arms are dominated by thrust that neither one models. The two arms differ by meters; the errors are kilometers.
mechanisms.evidence: Median |FFM - AP| at days 1 / 3 / 7, against the median AP error: SES-15 5.1 / 7.9 / 21.4 m against 6.0 / 12.0 / 30.2 km; Eutelsat 117 West B 8.2 / 18.1 / 54.5 m against 2.1 / 6.2 / 20.8 km; Galaxy 30 6.6 / 9.4 / 33 m against 2.5 / 9.3 / 21.5 km. The relative difference is 0.06-0.34 %. From hourly WAAS burn peaks (scripts/burn-times.mjs, burns-waas-hourly.json): SES-15's semimajor axis moves a median 452 m per sidereal day, and Eutelsat 117 West B's moves 112 m with 1.9 mdeg of plane change per day. Both thrust almost continuously. Galaxy 30 burns north-south about weekly (09-02, 09-08, 09-16, 09-23, 09-30, 10-07, 10-14, 10-21, 10-28) and east-west near 09-05, 09-13, 09-26 and 10-11. The registered day rule (burns-waas.json) misses half of the north-south burns.

mechanisms.claim: WA Galaxy 30, burn-free leads (19 rows): FFM loses by tens of meters because it fits the SRP coefficient on 24 h of noisy broadcast truth.
mechanisms.evidence: On the 2026-10-02 24 h window, the FFM fit leaves 11.5 m per axis (chi-square 1.32), and the fitted SRP is 0.0345 against AP's 0.0322. Holding SRP at 0.0322 gives 24.7 / 34.0 / 42.6 m at days 1 / 2 / 3, against AP 28.0 / 34.6 / 29.7 and the stored 43.4 / 84.8 / 112.8. Days 1 and 2 are removed; day 3 still loses. ECOM2 and in-track terms are ill-conditioned on this arc: ecom5 stalled at 128 m on day 1, in-track gave 711 m. One window only.

mechanisms.claim: No loss in GD, GE, IG or GN is a maneuver. Storms cannot act on either arm in these regimes.
mechanisms.evidence: LAGEOS and LARES-2 are passive spheres. On the GE satellites C006, C016, C020 and C217, the registered burn rule finds no burns (burns-beidou.json); only 7 GE loss rows overlap a registered burn. FFM flies no drag above 8,400 km, and AP's BTERM is held at 0.0005. Removing a GE, IG or GN loss needed only an SRP change, never a maneuver.

fixes.change: Cap maxStep by orbital period instead of the 8,400 km split, for example min(300 s, period/100), which is 120 s at LAGEOS. Turn solidTides on for orbits above 8,400 km.
fixes.expected: GD day-7 FFM median falls from 19 m to about 4-7 m, at or below AP's 12 m. Normal error falls about 10x. Navigation and GEO do not move: 300 s is under 1/144 of their periods. A registration must show, on new GD dates, a paired FFM-minus-AP day-7 interval below zero, Etalon unchanged, and no navigation cell moving beyond CHEAPER's 0.005 / 0.020 km margins. The production catalog already runs 120 s steps, tolerance 1e-14 and tides (propagator/ffm/catalog-configuration.mjs:30, 72-80).
fixes.cells: AP6/AP7 regimes 72 h, group GD, days 1-7 (the 54 % worse cell at day 7)

fixes.module: experiments harness lib/fit.mjs:21 and lib/frame.mjs:20-46 (analysis/estimation callers); propagator/ffm already accepts the kinds (catalog-configuration.mjs:120-127, force_models.cpp:536-550)
fixes.change: Fit ECOM2 Y0, B0, B1c and B1s beside the cannonball for every GNSS and GEO/IGSO bus, with priors of about 1e-8 m/s^2. The harness today knows only 4 parameter kinds and has no ECOM2 field. A working path is in scratch: scripts/fit2.mjs (ecomFrame) and scripts/host2.mjs. A smaller alternative for Galileo FOC alone is the fixed Y0 = +6.85e-10 already designed in results/ffm-galileo-y-bias.
fixes.expected: E218 day 7 falls from 0.1-0.3 km to 2-9 m. GPS and GLONASS day-7 losses go. GE and IG cells that are 60-69 % worse at days 3-7 turn into wins (C020 day 7 from 0.26 km to 0.01-0.06 km). Fit chi-square falls 10-20x. A registration must show, on new GN, GE and IG dates, ECOM2 FFM beating both AP and cannonball FFM at days 1-7 with paired intervals below zero, and no harm on Etalon or LAGEOS. Do not apply this to 24 h arcs of WAAS broadcast truth; it is ill-conditioned there.
fixes.cells: AP7 truth2 GN 24 h and 72 h (all leads; E218 carries 334 of 498 loss rows); AP6 regimes GE and IG 72 h, days 2-7; GEO-TRUTH BeiDou lines

fixes.module: experiments/operator-theory WA reporting (geo-burns.mjs and the WA tables)
fixes.change: Use hourly burn peaks (the method in scratch burn-times.mjs) to split WA windows into burn and burn-free. Report burn-free leads separately. On burn-free Galaxy 30 24 h arcs, test an SRP prior or a held SRP value. No model change: the ties are thrust.
fixes.expected: The WA 50-69 % 'worse' cells at ratio 1.00 are reclassified as maneuver ties. Day-1 and day-2 losses on burn-free Galaxy 30 leads likely go once SRP is held. A registration must show a paired gain on burn-free leads only.
fixes.cells: regimes-wa 24 h and 72 h, all leads

unsettled: Why FFM drifts at a 300 s step even at tolerance 1e-10. It may be ordinary RK78 truncation at 0.14 rad per step that the per-step tolerance does not bound, or something in FFM's fast integration path (INTEGRATION_POLICY, catalog-configuration.mjs:110) bypassing the tolerance. Settling it needs a module-level test against an analytic Kepler orbit. The step-cap fix works either way.
Most rows are classed by their group, not tested one by one: 892 of 939. Rerun coverage: GD 8 windows, GE and IG 9, GN 5, WA 1. For GPS and GLONASS the SRP class rests on one window each.

Ocean tides could not be tested. The request with FES2004 at degree 20 was refused with 'OCEAN_TIDE_MAXIMUM_DEGREE must lie in [2, 50]' (prw_dynamics.cpp:376-378, modules 9a05d899b9), even though 20 is in range. I suspect a mismatch between the clone's PRW JS bindings and FFM 2.0.4's schema; frame.mjs:44 writes the degree but not the order. Not shown.

Shadow and penumbra in the GEO eclipse season were not isolated. FFM's cannonball shadow is hard-coded conical (force_models.cpp:471-472), so no rerun can switch it off. ECOM2 removes the GE losses without touching it.
IGSO maneuvers: no burn test exists for the IG group. QZS-2I J002 was not rerun.
WA Galaxy 30 burn-free leads: one window was tested, and day 3 still loses with SRP held. Broadcast noise of about 11.5 m per axis (the stated URA is 2 m) limits what any 24 h arc can show.
Box-wing attitude was not tested. FFM's GNSS box-wing covers GPS IIR, IIR-M and IIF only (gnss_srp.h:68-70), and the harness has no path to it.

Run accounting: 60 FFM fits. 57 are rows in rows-*.jsonl (one, fullx, was refused). 3 are fits in the diverge diagnostics, which flew one fitted product under up to 12 settings; those extra flights are not counted separately. AP refits were used for diagnostics only and reproduce the stored AP numbers exactly. Runs were under nice -n 10 at 1-minute load 7.9-16.6, with network fetch disabled for WAAS and dates capped to the cached days 242-306.
